intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon and evening immersed in the heart of Marrakech's UNESCO-listed medina. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians perform in the square, then wander through the historic souks buying spices, leather goods, and lanterns. With a late Day 1 arrival, skip this on arrival night and begin fresh on Day 2 morning when crowds are manageable and light is ideal for photography. Stay within walking distance by booking a riad inside the medina walls.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Overnight Camp at Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Journey to the iconic golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for a 2-night desert experience. Ride camels at sunset into a traditional Berber camp, enjoy a tagine dinner under a sky full of stars, and wake at dawn for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes. This is the cultural and natural highlight of any Marrakech-Sahara itinerary and worth allocating Days 3–5 to allow travel time and full immersion. Book a camp within the dunes themselves to minimize transfer time.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Explore two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks back to back, both located within the southern medina. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with intricate Moroccan tilework and carved cedar ceilings, while the Saadian Tombs offer a rare glimpse into the royal burial chambers of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty. Combine both in a half-day morning visit to beat the heat and crowds. Staying in a medina riad puts you within a 10-minute walk of both sites.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class with Market Visit
experiences.description: Join a small-group cooking class led by a local chef, beginning with a guided tour of the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as chicken bastilla, harira soup, and orange-blossom couscous. Classes typically run 4 hours and include a full sit-down meal. Choose a school located inside or adjacent to the medina to avoid long transfers, especially useful for Days 2 or 6 when you are based in Marrakech.

experiences.name: Aït Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Day Trip
experiences.description: En route to or from the Sahara on Days 3 or 5, stop at the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning fortified mud-brick village used as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue through the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, palm groves, and Berber villages. This route is a natural stop on the Marrakech-to-Merzouga road, eliminating any detour and maximizing your travel days efficiently.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the airport bus (Line 19, ~20 MAD) or a petit taxi (negotiate to ~70–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, located in the heart of the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a quick snack from a late-night street stall near Jemaa el-Fna square (msemen flatbread or harira soup, ~10–20 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) ready before leaving the airport – exchange a small amount at the airport bureau de change. Avoid unofficial taxi touts; use metered petit taxis or negotiate firmly. Hotel Aday is a budget-friendly riad steps from Jemaa el-Fna.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café (mint tea, msemen, amlou almond-argan dip, ~20–30 MAD). Then walk to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, snake charmers setting up, and locals heading to work. Explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only, free) and stroll through the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the Medina's souks – the labyrinthine markets selling spices, leather, textiles, and crafts. Visit the Spice Square (Rahba Kedima) and the dyers' souk. Head to the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), one of Morocco's most stunning examples of Islamic architecture, with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar wood. Nearby, visit the small but fascinating Museum of Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD, or combo ticket ~120 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Derb Sidi Bouloukat – mint tea, bread, olive oil, amlou (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Eat at a local hole-in-the-wall restaurant in the Medina – try a bowl of harira soup with bread and a hard-boiled egg (~15–25 MAD) or a kefta sandwich (~20 MAD)
meals.dinner: Head to Jemaa el-Fna food stalls in the evening – try merguez sausages, grilled brochettes, snail soup (babouche), and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget ~50–80 MAD for a full meal

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected in the souks – start at 40–50% of the asking price. Wear comfortable walking shoes; the Medina streets are uneven. The Ben Youssef Madrasa is a must-see and very photogenic in the morning light.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring beautifully decorated mausoleums. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Afterward, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) – explore its distinctive architecture, the Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation), and the covered market. Then visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate painted ceilings, mosaic floors, and lush gardens. Spend time wandering the palace's many rooms and courtyards.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a massive open-air spectacle – storytellers, musicians, acrobats, and henna artists. Climb to a rooftop café terrace overlooking the square for a mint tea and the best view of the chaos below (~20–30 MAD for tea).

meals.breakfast: Café des Épices area or hotel – café au lait and msemen (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Restaurant Haj Boujemaa near the Mellah – local tagine or couscous with vegetables (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls or a cheap Medina restaurant – try pastilla (pigeon pie) or a lamb tagine (~50–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book a shared grand taxi or budget tour to the Sahara (Day 4–6) tonight if not already arranged. Many budget tour operators near Jemaa el-Fna offer 3-day Sahara trips from ~800–1,200 MAD per person in a shared group. This is the most cost-effective way to reach Merzouga.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 07:00) from Marrakech by shared minibus or budget group tour toward the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The journey takes approximately 8–9 hours with stops. Cross the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) – stunning mountain scenery and Berber villages. Stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar/fortified village, ~15–20 MAD entry) – a breathtaking ancient mud-brick citadel used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley, passing palm groves, kasbahs, and rose-growing villages (the region is famous for its rose festival). Stop in Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Africa' – for a quick lunch and optional peek at the Atlas Film Studios exterior (free from outside). Continue driving through the Dades Valley and Todra Gorge area.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Merzouga village at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes as the sun sets. Check into a budget desert camp or auberge (~150–250 MAD per person). Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset camel trek into the dunes (usually included in budget tour packages). Watch the sun sink behind the golden dunes – an unforgettable experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure (~20–30 MAD) or packed snacks
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate – tagine or sandwich (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp – harira, tagine, bread, mint tea, and fresh fruit (~60–100 MAD or included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: Dress in layers – the Atlas Mountains can be cold in March, while the desert is warm by day but cold at night (temperatures can drop to 5–10°C). Bring a warm jacket, sunscreen, and a headscarf for the dunes. Confirm camel trek and camp dinner are included in your tour package before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 06:00) and climb the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot for a spectacular sunrise over the Sahara – one of Morocco's most magical moments. The silence, the shifting colors of the sand, and the vast emptiness are extraordinary. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast. Spend the late morning exploring Merzouga village on foot – visit the local market, chat with Tuareg nomads, and see the unique ecosystem where the desert meets a seasonal lake (Dayet Srji) that attracts flamingos in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional activities (budget-friendly): rent a quad bike to explore the dunes (~150–200 MAD/hour), visit a local Gnawa music family for a cultural performance (~30–50 MAD donation), or simply relax and read in the shade of the camp. In the late afternoon, take a short walk to the edge of the dunes to watch the light change on the sand – the colors shift from gold to orange to deep red.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Berber music and drumming session around a campfire under the stars. The Sahara sky at night is extraordinary with minimal light pollution – bring a star map app. Sleep in a traditional nomad tent or basic desert auberge.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at camp – bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, mint tea (~included or ~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Simple lunch at camp or in Merzouga village – tagine, salad, bread (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Communal Berber dinner at camp around the fire – couscous with seven vegetables or mechoui lamb (~60–100 MAD or included)

day_by_day.notes: March is an excellent time for the Sahara – days are warm (25–30°C) but not scorching like summer. Nights are cool so bring a sleeping bag or request extra blankets. Protect your camera and phone from sand. Bargain politely for any optional activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Merzouga (around 07:00–08:00) for the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route. Pass through the Todra Gorge – dramatic 300-meter-high limestone canyon walls with a river running through. Stop for a short walk through the gorge (free entry, ~30–45 minutes). Continue through the Dades Gorge and the Valley of Roses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in the town of Kelaat M'Gouna (Rose Valley) – famous for its rose water and rose products. Browse the local cooperative shops for affordable rose water, soap, and cosmetics (great budget souvenirs, ~20–50 MAD). Continue driving back through the Atlas Mountains. Arrive back in Marrakech in the late afternoon/early evening (around 17:00–19:00 depending on stops).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Aday, shower, and rest. Head out for a final evening stroll through the Medina. Visit the Mouassine Fountain area and the trendy Mouassine neighborhood for a quieter, more local atmosphere. Browse the artisan shops for last-minute souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at camp before departure (~included or ~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant in the Dades Valley – tagine with local bread (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech – try Restaurant Souk Kafe or a local Medina eatery near the hotel for a proper sit-down meal: pastilla, tagine, or mechoui (~60–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return route through Todra Gorge and Dades Valley is equally scenic and worth the extra stops. Buy rose water products directly from women's cooperatives to ensure fair trade pricing. Keep energy snacks and water for the long drive.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~70 MAD, or ~150 MAD including the Berber Museum inside), a stunning botanical garden with electric-blue buildings, exotic plants, and the YSL Museum nearby. Arrive early (opens at 08:00) to avoid crowds. The garden was restored by Yves Saint Laurent and is one of Marrakech's most beautiful spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks – look for argan oil, saffron, ras el hanout spice mix, leather goods, and handmade pottery. Head to the Ensemble Artisanal (government-run craft center near the Koutoubia) for fixed, fair prices if you want to avoid bargaining. Grab a final mint tea at a rooftop café. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure flight, take a petit taxi or bus to Marrakech Menara Airport (~70–100 MAD by taxi, ~20 MAD by bus Line 19). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert, history, and food.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast near the hotel – café au lait, msemen, honey, and amlou (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café near Majorelle Garden or a quick bite in the Gueliz neighborhood (the modern French-influenced district) – sandwich or salad (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a final street food snack near Jemaa el-Fna before heading to the airport – orange juice and a kefta sandwich (~30–40 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is very popular – book tickets online in advance if possible to skip the queue. The Gueliz neighborhood offers a different, more modern side of Marrakech worth a quick explore. Keep ~200–300 MAD in cash for taxi, tips, and last-minute purchases. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and pre-booked tours): approximately 2,500–3,500 MAD (~$250–$350 USD) per person, including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Hotel Aday, freshen up, and settle into your riad-style accommodation in the medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in-flight or transit.
day_by_day.evening: Upon arrival after 22:30: Take a short stroll along the quiet lantern-lit alleyways of Derb Sidi Bouloukat to decompress. Grab a light late-night snack near the hotel if hunger strikes — many small cafés near Jemaa el-Fna stay open past midnight.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night snack near the hotel — try a bowl of harira soup or a msemen flatbread from a nearby street stall (budget-friendly, ~30–50 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 22:30. Allow 45–60 minutes for immigration, baggage, and a taxi or transfer to the medina. Hotel Aday is inside the medina; confirm with the hotel in advance for late-night check-in instructions and directions through the narrow derbs (alleyways). Keep some Moroccan dirhams handy for the taxi (~150–200 MAD from Marrakech Menara Airport).

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely riad breakfast at the hotel. Afterward, walk 10 minutes to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers set up early. Then visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque (exterior viewing) and stroll through the surrounding gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan craftsmanship and lush courtyards. Afterward, wander through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the adjacent Mellah Market for a glimpse into Marrakech's layered history. Stop at the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD) for panoramic rooftop views.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle — musicians, acrobats, and dozens of food stalls fill the square. Enjoy dinner at one of the square's communal food stalls for an authentic, lively experience.

meals.breakfast: Included at Hotel Aday or a nearby café — mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (almond-argan dip).
meals.lunch: Café Arabe or a local restaurant near Bahia Palace — try a lamb tagine or chicken bastilla (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna night market food stalls — grilled merguez sausages, kefta skewers, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~60–100 MAD total).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the medina streets are cobblestoned and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks. Keep your belongings secure in the busy square. March weather in Marrakech is mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket for the evening is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Then explore the Marrakech Museum housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace (~50 MAD) — excellent exhibits on Moroccan art, ceramics, and history. Wander through the adjacent Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), one of North Africa's most stunning Islamic schools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon getting lost in the souks — the labyrinthine markets organized by craft: spice souk, leather souk, lantern souk, and textile souk. Hire a local guide from the medina association (~150–200 MAD/hour) for context and to avoid getting lost. Visit a traditional tannery for a bird's-eye view of the leather dyeing process.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a rooftop dinner with views over the medina skyline as the call to prayer echoes across the city.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or Café des Épices near the spice square — coffee, fresh juice, and Moroccan pancakes.
meals.lunch: Local hole-in-the-wall near the souks — try a harira soup, a kefta sandwich, or a vegetable couscous (~40–70 MAD).
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant (rooftop, mid-range) — modern Moroccan cuisine with panoramic medina views (~150–200 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa and Saadian Tombs are close to each other — plan them together to save walking time. Arrive at the Saadian Tombs early to beat crowds. In the souks, be politely firm if not interested in buying — shopkeepers are persistent but friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a private or shared transfer through the dramatic Draa Valley and Dades Gorge. The drive passes through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) — stop for photos at the summit and visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou kasbah (entry ~10 MAD), a breathtaking fortified village used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Valley of Roses (Dadès Valley) and the Draa Valley — a landscape of red kasbahs, palm oases, and dramatic gorges. Arrive in the Dades Gorge area by late afternoon. Check in to a mid-range guesthouse (maison d'hôte) carved into the gorge cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset walk into the Dades Gorge — the rock formations glow amber and crimson at dusk. Return to the guesthouse for a traditional Berber dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Aït Benhaddou — lamb tagine or vegetable couscous with fresh bread (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: At the guesthouse — a full Berber spread: harira, tagine, couscous, and fresh fruit (~100–150 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~6–7 hours total with stops). Book a private driver or join a shared desert tour from Marrakech in advance (~400–600 MAD per person for shared, ~1,200–1,800 MAD for private). The Tizi n'Tichka pass can be cold in March — bring a layer. Aït Benhaddou is a must-stop and worth 1–1.5 hours of exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early to watch the sunrise paint the Dades Gorge in golden light. After breakfast, continue the drive toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes — the gateway to the Sahara. Stop at the Todra Gorge en route, a spectacular 300-meter-high canyon carved by the Todra River — walk through the narrow gorge floor (free, ~1 hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Merzouga by early afternoon. Check in to a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse at the edge of the dunes. Rest and prepare for the desert experience. Optional: visit a local Gnawa musician's home for a traditional music session (~50–100 MAD tip).
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes (~200–300 MAD per person). Arrive at a desert camp for an unforgettable night — Berber music around a campfire, a sky exploding with stars, and the profound silence of the Sahara. Sleep in a comfortable furnished tent.

meals.breakfast: At the Dades guesthouse — Moroccan breakfast with fresh-baked bread and argan oil.
meals.lunch: Simple lunch at a café in Tinghir near Todra Gorge — tagine or sandwich (~60–90 MAD).
meals.dinner: At the desert camp — traditional Berber dinner: lentil soup, slow-cooked lamb tagine, and mint tea by the fire (typically included in camp package).

day_by_day.notes: Book your desert camp in advance — mid-range camps with private tents and en-suite facilities cost ~400–700 MAD per person including dinner and breakfast. March nights in the Sahara can drop to 5–8°C — pack a warm layer and socks. The camel ride is optional but highly recommended. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn to climb a dune and watch the Sahara sunrise — one of the most spectacular sights in Morocco. After breakfast at the camp, explore the dunes on foot or by sandboard (~50 MAD rental). Visit the small village of Khemliya nearby to meet the Gnawa community and learn about their music and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via the scenic southern route through Rissani (historic market town and gateway to the Tafilalet oasis), Erfoud (fossil capital of Morocco — visit a fossil workshop), and the Ziz Valley with its stunning palm grove stretching for kilometers. Stop for photos and a mint tea break.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Ouarzazate area by evening. Check in to a mid-range hotel. Stroll through the town and visit the Atlas Film Studios (exterior view at dusk — the world's largest film studio). Enjoy a relaxed dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: At the desert camp — Berber breakfast with msemen, honey, and mint tea (included in camp package).
meals.lunch: Roadside café in Rissani or Erfoud — try a camel burger (a local specialty!) or a lamb tagine (~70–100 MAD).
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Ouarzazate — Moroccan cuisine with a relaxed atmosphere (~120–180 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Merzouga to Ouarzazate is approximately 4–5 hours with stops. If time allows, a quick visit inside the Atlas Film Studios (~60 MAD) is worthwhile for film and history enthusiasts. Ouarzazate is known as the 'Hollywood of Africa' and has hosted productions including Lawrence of Arabia and The Mummy.

day_by_day.morning: Drive back to Marrakech via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (approximately 3.5–4 hours). Arrive in Marrakech by midday. Drop bags at Hotel Aday and head to the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD) — a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent, featuring the iconic cobalt-blue villa and the Berber Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Yves Saint Laurent Museum adjacent to Majorelle Garden (~100 MAD) for a fascinating look at the designer's love affair with Morocco. Spend your final afternoon doing last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — argan oil, leather goods, spices, and handwoven textiles make excellent gifts. Enjoy a traditional hammam experience at a local mid-range hammam (~150–250 MAD for the full scrub treatment).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final evening in Marrakech with a special dinner at a traditional riad restaurant — a fitting farewell to Morocco's rich culinary culture. Return to Hotel Aday to pack and rest before any onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Ouarzazate before departure — café au lait, croissant, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Upon return to Marrakech — Le Jardin restaurant near the souks, a beautiful garden café (~120–160 MAD).
meals.dinner: Riad Yima or a similar traditional riad restaurant — a full Moroccan feast: pastilla, tagine, couscous, and bastilla au lait dessert (~200–280 MAD per person for a special farewell meal).

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden can get crowded by midday — arrive as early as possible. Book the hammam in advance or ask Hotel Aday for a trusted local recommendation. If departing the next day, confirm your airport transfer the night before. The medina can be disorienting at night — save your hotel's GPS coordinates offline. End your trip with a final glass of mint tea on a rooftop — a perfect Moroccan goodbye.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Private airport transfer arranged with a luxury chauffeur service to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony and a light late-night snack prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival (22:30). Check in to Hotel Aday, freshen up, and enjoy the hotel's curated welcome amenities — traditional pastries, argan oil toiletries, and a chilled bottle of Moroccan rosé or fresh juice. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome spread at Hotel Aday: Moroccan briouats, olives, fresh bread, honey, and herbal tea arranged by the hotel upon request

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Hotel Aday. Keep Day 1 light — no sightseeing. The Medina streets near Derb Sidi Bouloukat can be narrow; ensure the driver knows the nearest vehicle drop-off point.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel rooftop. At 10:00, begin a private guided walking tour of the Marrakech Medina — explore the labyrinthine souks of Souk Semmarine and Souk El Attarine, visit the historic Medersa Ben Youssef (one of North Africa's finest Islamic colleges), and discover the ancient Almoravid Koubba. Your private guide will provide rich historical context throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (14th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture) followed by a stop at the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the ornate Saadian Tombs — royal necropolis dating to the 16th century. Afterward, enjoy a private hammam and spa experience at a premium riad spa near the Medina for full relaxation and cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk to witness the magical transformation — snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians fill the square. Dine at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the square for a cinematic Marrakech experience.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday: msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (argan oil and almond spread), fresh orange juice, mint tea, soft-boiled eggs, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, near Rahba Kedima) — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the lamb pastilla and harira soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin (Mouassine neighborhood) — elegant garden restaurant set in a 16th-century riad; signature dishes include slow-cooked lamb tagine and bastilla au pigeon

day_by_day.notes: Book Medersa Ben Youssef and Saadian Tombs tickets in advance to avoid queues. The private hammam session should be pre-booked — recommended: Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart by private luxury 4x4 vehicle toward the Ourika Valley in the Atlas Mountains (approximately 1 hour from Marrakech). Explore the lush Berber villages, terraced gardens, and the cascading Setti Fatma waterfalls. Engage with a local Berber family for an authentic cultural exchange — learn about traditional weaving and mountain life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return toward Marrakech and stop at the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (Jardin Majorelle) — a cobalt-blue botanical masterpiece once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the Islamic Art Museum of Marrakech within the garden complex. Afterward, visit the nearby Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech for a world-class fashion and art experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina for an exclusive private cooking class at a premium riad kitchen — learn to prepare a traditional Moroccan feast: harira soup, chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and orange blossom pastilla for dessert. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional Berber restaurant in Ourika Valley — freshly baked bread from a clay oven, Berber omelette, mountain honey, and mint tea with panoramic Atlas views
meals.dinner: Private cooking class dinner at a premium riad — multi-course Moroccan feast you prepare yourself with a master chef; paired with Moroccan wines or fresh juices

day_by_day.notes: The Ourika Valley road can be winding — motion sickness tablets recommended if sensitive. Majorelle Garden is very popular; arrive early afternoon to avoid peak crowds. The private cooking class should be booked in advance — recommended providers: La Maison Arabe Cooking School or Souk Cuisine.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure at 07:00 by private luxury 4x4 for the epic journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dunes — approximately 8–9 hours with scenic stops). Cross the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) through the High Atlas Mountains with breathtaking panoramic views. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — a magnificent 11th-century ksar (fortified village) used as a filming location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Dadès Valley) and the dramatic Gorges du Dadès — towering red rock formations carved by ancient rivers. Stop for photos and a brief walk through the gorge. Continue through the Draa Valley's palm groves and kasbahs toward Merzouga.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga at sunset. Mount private camels (or opt for a 4x4 dune buggy) for a guided sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the tallest dunes in Morocco reaching 150m. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp for a night under the Saharan stars.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast prepared by Hotel Aday before departure — Moroccan pastries, fruit, and thermos of mint tea for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — traditional Moroccan tagine, fresh salads, and Berber bread baked in a clay oven
meals.dinner: Exclusive dinner at the luxury desert camp — traditional Moroccan feast served under the stars: harira, mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous with seven vegetables, and Moroccan pastries; live Gnawa music and drumming performance around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — depart early. Ensure the private driver is experienced with mountain roads. Aït Benhaddou entry fee is minimal but a guide is recommended. Luxury desert camp recommendation: Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp — pre-book well in advance. Pack warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf for sand.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private guided sunrise hike to the top of the highest Erg Chebbi dune — witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises as golden light floods the endless sea of sand. Return to camp for a lavish Saharan breakfast. Explore the surrounding desert on foot or by camel, visit a local nomadic Berber family encampment, and learn about traditional desert life, navigation by stars, and medicinal desert plants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert camp and journey toward the Todra Gorge — dramatic 300m-high limestone canyon walls. Take a guided walk through the narrow gorge floor where a cool river runs between the towering cliffs. Continue toward Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — and visit the Atlas Film Studios, the world's largest film studio, where Lawrence of Arabia, Babel, and many others were filmed.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate (recommended: Dar Ahlam or Ksar Char-Bagh). Enjoy a sunset aperitif on the terrace overlooking the Draa Valley. Dine at the hotel's gourmet restaurant for a refined evening.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Saharan breakfast at the desert camp — fresh bread, honey, argan oil, Berber omelette, dates, fresh fruit, and mint tea served in the open desert
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant near Todra Gorge — grilled kefta, Moroccan salads, and fresh-squeezed orange juice with gorge views
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at your luxury kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate — refined Moroccan-French fusion cuisine; signature dishes may include pigeon pastilla, lamb with prunes and almonds, and saffron crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune climb is steep — wear closed-toe shoes. Todra Gorge is best visited in the afternoon when light enters the canyon. Atlas Film Studios tours run throughout the day — no advance booking required but a private guide enhances the experience. Ouarzazate luxury accommodation must be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Ouarzazate — explore the Taourirt Kasbah, a stunning 19th-century fortified palace and UNESCO heritage site once belonging to the powerful Glaoui clan. Wander through the adjacent ksar village still inhabited by local families. Visit the Ouarzazate Museum of Cinema for fascinating behind-the-scenes history of the region's film legacy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Ouarzazate and return to Marrakech via the scenic Tizi n'Tichka pass (approximately 4 hours). Stop at artisan cooperatives along the route to browse and purchase premium Moroccan crafts — hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, and fossils. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back in to Hotel Aday and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner experience at one of Marrakech's most celebrated restaurants — a multi-course tasting menu in a beautifully restored 17th-century riad setting with live Andalusian music. End the evening with a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated Koutoubia Mosque.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the luxury kasbah hotel in Ouarzazate — full spread including Moroccan pancakes, fresh juices, local cheeses, and pastries
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop at a scenic mountain restaurant on the Tizi n'Tichka pass — hearty Berber tagine and fresh mountain bread
meals.dinner: Premium tasting menu dinner at La Maison Arabe or Dar Yacout, Marrakech — iconic riad dining experience with courses including bastilla, mechoui, and traditional Moroccan desserts; wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Taourirt Kasbah is a short walk from the town center. The return drive over Tizi n'Tichka is stunning but winding — allow extra time. Dar Yacout and La Maison Arabe require advance reservations — book at least 2–3 weeks ahead. The Koutoubia Mosque is beautifully lit at night and visible from many rooftop bars in the Medina.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace described as the 'eighth wonder of the world,' now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with resident storks. Explore the adjacent Mellah market for last-minute premium souvenirs: saffron, argan oil, rose water, and hand-crafted leather goods from the famous Chouara Tannery viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a final luxury spa afternoon at a premium hammam — full traditional hammam ritual with black soap, kessa exfoliation, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Recommended: Hammam de la Rose or Royal Mansour Spa (day access). Return to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a final sunset dinner at a rooftop restaurant near Djemaa el-Fna — savoring last views of the Koutoubia minaret and the Atlas Mountains on the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent breakfast at Hotel Aday — full traditional Moroccan spread with fresh-squeezed orange juice, msemen, honey, amlou, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (Rahba Kedima square) — relaxed rooftop setting with views over the spice market; try the zaalouk, kefta sandwich, and fresh lemonade with orange blossom
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Terrasse des Épices or Kechmara — elegant rooftop dining with panoramic Medina views; order the slow-cooked lamb shank, Moroccan mezze platter, and traditional mint tea ceremony to close the trip

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy on weekends. Purchase saffron and argan oil from certified cooperatives to ensure authenticity. The hammam session should be booked the day before. Keep some Moroccan dirhams for tips and last-minute market purchases — many vendors do not accept cards.
